cities.name: Agartala
cities.overview: Tripura's capital, close to the Bangladesh border, a relaxed city built around the royal palace of the Manikya kings.
cities.history: The Manikya kings moved here from Udaipur in the 18th and 19th centuries. It joined India in 1949, and it's now 2 km from the Bangladesh border.

cities.name: Melaghar
cities.overview: A town in Sipahijala district on the shore of Rudrasagar Lake, about 55 km from Agartala.

cities.name: Kailashahar
cities.overview: A town in northern Tripura, the headquarters of Unakoti district and an old seat of the Tripuri kings.

cities.name: Udaipur
cities.overview: The old capital of the Manikya kingdom, known as the Lake City, with the famous Tripura Sundari Temple.

cities.name: Kumarghat
cities.overview: A northern town on the road to the Jampui Hills.

cities.name: Belonia
cities.overview: A town in South Tripura, close to the Pilak ruins and the Trishna forest.

places.name: Ujjayanta Palace
places.shortDescription: The white Indo-Saracenic palace of Tripura's kings, now the state museum, set behind Mughal-style gardens.
places.description: Ujjayanta Palace faces a pair of lakes and formal gardens in the centre of Agartala, its domes and towers gleaming white. Since 2013 it has housed the Tripura State Museum, with galleries on the state's tribal communities, royal history and the art of Northeast India. The tiled floors, carved doors and great hall reflect the palace's grandeur. The grounds are lit up in the evening.
places.history: Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya built the palace between 1899 and 1901. Rabindranath Tagore, a friend of the royal family, is said to have suggested its name. It served as the state legislative assembly building until 2011.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee for the museum; extra for cameras.

places.name: Neermahal
places.shortDescription: A royal summer palace rising from the middle of Rudrasagar Lake, reached by boat.
places.description: Neermahal, the water palace, stands in Rudrasagar Lake, its red-and-white domes and pavilions blending Hindu and Mughal styles. Boats from the Melaghar jetty take about 15 minutes to reach it. Inside are courtyards, a royal open-air stage and terraces overlooking the water. The lake hosts migratory birds in winter, and the Neermahal Water Festival with boat races is held in August.
places.history: Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya built the palace as a summer residence; it was completed in 1938. It is the largest of only two water palaces in India.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; August for the Neermahal Water Festival.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee plus boat fare from Melaghar.

location.address: Rudrasagar Lake, Melaghar, Sipahijala district, Tripura 799115

places.name: Unakoti
places.shortDescription: Giant rock-cut carvings of Shiva and other deities hidden in a forested hillside in north Tripura.
places.description: Unakoti is a forested hill where enormous figures are carved into the rock faces and boulders along a stream. The most striking is the Unakotishvara Kal Bhairava, a head of Shiva about 10 m tall with an elaborate headdress, flanked by goddesses. Hundreds of smaller images of Ganesha, Durga, Vishnu and others lie scattered around the site. Steps and paths lead down through the forest. The Ashokastami fair in March–April draws large crowds.
places.history: The carvings are generally dated to the 7th–9th centuries CE. Legend says Shiva cursed a crore minus one gods to turn to stone here, giving the site its name, 'one less than a crore'. It is on UNESCO's tentative list.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; the Ashokastami fair is in March or April.

location.address: Unakoti, near Kailashahar, Unakoti district, Tripura 799277

places.name: Tripura Sundari Temple
places.shortDescription: A key Shakti Peetha at Udaipur, on a hill shaped like a tortoise, with a large sacred tank.
places.description: A small, red-and-yellow Bengali-style temple, whose tank is full of large fish and turtles. A big fair is held here at Diwali.
places.history: Built by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in 1501.

places.name: Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A sanctuary close to Agartala, known for its clouded leopards and spectacled langurs.
places.description: A small, well-used forest with a zoo, lakes and boating. Its clouded leopard enclosures are the main draw.

places.name: Rudrasagar Lake
places.shortDescription: A wetland lake at Melaghar, with the Neermahal water palace at its centre.
places.description: A big natural reservoir, listed as a Ramsar site, that's popular for its winter birds and boat rides to the water palace.

places.name: Jampui Hills
places.shortDescription: The highest hills in Tripura, a Mizo-populated range with orange orchards and a spring in the air.
places.description: A quiet range of tea, orange orchards and tribal villages. The Orange Festival every November is the highlight.

places.name: Trishna Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A sanctuary in South Tripura known for its gaur, spectacled langurs and birdlife.
places.description: A forest of low hills and marsh, close to the town of Belonia. Gaur are the main attraction here.

places.name: Pilak
places.shortDescription: An archaeological site in South Tripura, with Hindu and Buddhist images dating from the 8th century.
places.description: Terracotta plaques and Buddhist and Hindu sculptures found across a wide area show the region's links with the Bengal plains.
